items.title: 〇(11/10)。くた・れAI 。AI依存症になるな ! AIを恋人にするな ！　AIを使うな、自分で考えて文章を書け ! !
items.summary:
〇(11/10)。くた・れAI 。AI依存症になるな ! AIを恋人にするな ！　AIを使うな、自分で考えて文章を書け ! !

AIに惑わされるな！ AIに問うな、本文を読み、自分で考えて、文章を書け ！！

原告の請求一部容認、（被告の権利一部を取り消す）。

知的財産高等裁判所により「権利一部を取り消す」とされた３７１件目のものです。

https://t.co/leY9QDuVUM

https://t.co/bCSKee45dM

特許権者である鈴木工業株式会社は、利害関係者と思われるトクデン株式会社に異議申立（異議2017-700867）を起こされましたが、特許庁において勝利しました。

また、トクデン株式会社は別途、無効審判（審判2022-800026）を起こしましたがこれも又、特許権者の勝利に終わっています。

トクデン株式会社はこれを不服として知的財産高等裁判所に訴えました。

知的財産高等裁判所においては、「特許庁が無効２０２２－８０００２６号事件について令和５年８月１７日にした審決において審判の請求は成り立たないとした部分のうち、特許第６１１４４３５号の請求項１及び４から６までに係る部分を取り消す。」され、特許権の一部が取り消されました。

更に、「本件発明１及び４から６までについて進歩性を認めた審決の判断は誤りであり、原告の主張する本件審決の取消事由のうち、本件発明１に係る進歩性欠如、本件発明４に係る進歩性欠如、本件5 発明５に係る進歩性欠如及び本件発明６に係る進歩性欠如は認められると判断する。」としています。

その結果、特許権は【請求項２】と【請求項３】とが残ったようです。

ここで特許庁における審査段階を振り返ってみます。

特許庁の審判官（宮崎光治）は、特開平０５－１９８３７０号公報を含めて５件の引用文献と参考特許文献を出願人に提示しています。

一方、知的財産高等裁判所においては、無効審判（2022-800026）で審判請求人より提示された（甲第１号証：米国再発行特許発明第３６７８７号明細書）を含む５件（甲１号証〜甲５号証）が提示されています。

そして、これら甲１号証〜甲５号証をもって、「特許第６１１４４３５号の請求項１及び４から６までに係る部分を取り消す。」とされました。

特許庁の審判官（宮崎光治）は、何故これら甲１号証〜甲５号証を見つけることができなかったのでしょうか。

ここでも、特許庁の審査官の調査能力が弱いことが証明されています。

更に、異議審判においては、甲第１号証：特開２００９－２７２２９５号公報を含む４件が異議申立人より提示されていますが、特許庁の審判官（田村嘉章ら）は「特許第６１１４４３５号の請求項１ないし６に係る特許を維持する。」として、知的財産高等裁判所の判断とは異なる結論をしています。

特許庁の審査段階における審査官のいい加減な（サーチ）に基づいた、特許付与は許されません。

更には、特許庁の審判においても誤った判断により特許権の維持を行なったのも、これまた許されません。

従って、本来なら、鈴木工業株式会社の出願に対して、特許庁は特許を与えるべきでなかった、と考えます。

ここで、本件特許公開（特開2017-199613）の「出願情報」のうち「ＦＩ」と「Ｆターム」を、本エクセル資料の２シート目以降に挙げておきました。

そしてまた、「検索用語・分類（ＦＩ、Ｆターム）の選定 と 検索論理式の作成」、「その具体例」、「登録調査機関の検索者が行った、不十分で、的外れな「論理検索式」による（サーチ）」、「登録調査機関（株式会社ＡＩＲＩ）の検索者が見つけることのできなかった特許文献」などの資料を添付します。

items.title: AI and your job: Threat or opportunity?
items.summary:
MOBILE, Ala. (WALA) - Artificial intelligence is becoming a bigger part of everyday life, raising questions about what the technology could mean for workers and their jobs.

Some economists believe AI poses a particular threat to entry-level and repetitive work, including call center, data entry and junior copywriting jobs, according to The Wall Street Journal. Those tasks may be easier to automate. [...] But AI could also create opportunities. A Bloomberg article points to potential job growth in construction and manufacturing as companies build data centers and produce the chips that power the technology. Some higher-skilled office workers could also benefit if AI helps them become more productive. [...] The long-term impact on jobs remains unclear, but workers can take steps to prepare. Exploring AI chatbots, writing assistants and other tools may help people find ways to work more efficiently and develop skills that complement the technology.

items.title: Google AI policy forces decision for San Diego schools – NBC 7 San Diego
items.summary:
As districts consider their options, students are already seeing artificial intelligence become a more common part of everyday learning.

“I feel like I see a lot of people using AI now,” said Delilah Ortiz, a student at El Camino High School.

Some students believe the focus should be on establishing guidelines for AI use rather than banning the technology entirely. [...] San Diego County school districts face a January deadline to decide whether to opt in to Google's artificial intelligence features or lose access to the company's search engine, forcing educators to weigh the benefits of AI against concerns about student access to the technology. [...] Google plans to disable a range of AI-powered features, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search in January to give school districts more control over the technology students can access. However, districts that want to continue using Google Search will have to opt in to the AI features.

items.title: Military-made AI tool helped thwart World Cup bomb threat - Federal News Network
items.summary:
The 2026 World Cup brought more than six million spectators from around the world to more than 100 matches in 16 host cities in the U.S., Canada and Mexico over the course of two months, prompting a massive interagency effort to secure those sites using technologies like AI and drones. Two people were charged in connection with another bomb threat against FIFA during a World Cup match at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. [...] A military-made artificial intelligence tool helped law enforcement thwart a bomb threat at the FIFA World Cup in California this summer.

The previously undisclosed incident occurred June 18, when Switzerland faced Bosnia and Herzegovina at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles, Army Capt. Ryan Hetrick, who leads the Pentagon’s Generative AI Task Force, said Nov. 6 at an AI event in Washington. [...] Hetrick has become one of the military’s biggest — and busiest — evangelists for AI. The GenAI Task Force travels around the globe to sit down with troops on operations floors and in the field and find AI fixes for their most pressing problems.

items.title: Australia to mandate AI breach reporting, create regulator after OpenAI breach | Reuters

However, both companies told Australian parliament last ​month that they would welcome ​laws requiring them to ⁠report data breaches carried out by their AI agents, acknowledging the decision to notify was currently at their discretion.

Albanese said his centre-left ​Labor government would set up an AI regulator to oversee security ​controls throughout ⁠the development and deployment of AI systems, identify serious risks and conduct independent evaluations of AI models. [...] "The AI safety regulator will be able to enforce significant penalties for AI companies ⁠doing the ​wrong thing," he said.

The mandatory AI safety and ​security protections will form part of the government's proposed AI legislation, Albanese said, which it plans to introduce in ​Parliament next year.

Reporting by Renju Jose in Sydney; Editing by Christian Schmollinger and Saad Sayeed

Our Standards: The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles. [...] OpenAI has said it learned of the breach only in August ​and that the incident was unintentional. Its review found no evidence that patient records were accessed by ‌the ⁠agent.

The breach has added to friction between Australia and US technology companies, after Canberra refused ChatGPT maker OpenAI and rival Anthropic exemptions from copyright laws for model training, instead requiring them to negotiate licensing agreements with Australian rights holders.

This is f*cking insane. Geoffrey Hinton, the Nobel Prize winner they call the Godfather of AI, was asked what AI will do to jobs. His answer:

"For mundane intellectual labor, AI is just going to replace everybody"

In 93 seconds, he explains why this time is different: one person with an AI assistant will do the work of 10

The new jobs everyone promises? If AI can do all routine thinking work, he asks what jobs are left to create

Then the part that hits hardest. His niece answers complaint letters for a health service. Each one took her 25 minutes. Now AI writes it, she checks it, and it takes 5. So they need five times fewer of her

He agrees it won't be AI that takes your job, it'll be a person using AI. That just means far fewer people

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \) là một hàm mà khi lấy đạo hàm sẽ cho ra \( x^2 \). Nguyên hàm của \( x^n \) (với \( n \neq -1 \)) được tính theo công thức:

\[
\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C
\]

Trong trường hợp này, với \( n = 2 \):

\[
\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

Vậy nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \) là:

\[
\frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

Trong đó \( C \) là hằng số tích phân.

items.title: AI and your job: Threat or opportunity?
items.summary:
MOBILE, Ala. (WALA) - Artificial intelligence is becoming a bigger part of everyday life, raising questions about what the technology could mean for workers and their jobs.

Some economists believe AI poses a particular threat to entry-level and repetitive work, including call center, data entry and junior copywriting jobs, according to The Wall Street Journal. Those tasks may be easier to automate. [...] But AI could also create opportunities. A Bloomberg article points to potential job growth in construction and manufacturing as companies build data centers and produce the chips that power the technology. Some higher-skilled office workers could also benefit if AI helps them become more productive. [...] The long-term impact on jobs remains unclear, but workers can take steps to prepare. Exploring AI chatbots, writing assistants and other tools may help people find ways to work more efficiently and develop skills that complement the technology.

items.title: Google AI policy forces decision for San Diego schools – NBC 7 San Diego
items.summary:
As districts consider their options, students are already seeing artificial intelligence become a more common part of everyday learning.

“I feel like I see a lot of people using AI now,” said Delilah Ortiz, a student at El Camino High School.

Some students believe the focus should be on establishing guidelines for AI use rather than banning the technology entirely. [...] San Diego County school districts face a January deadline to decide whether to opt in to Google's artificial intelligence features or lose access to the company's search engine, forcing educators to weigh the benefits of AI against concerns about student access to the technology. [...] Google plans to disable a range of AI-powered features, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search in January to give school districts more control over the technology students can access. However, districts that want to continue using Google Search will have to opt in to the AI features.

items.title: Military-made AI tool helped thwart World Cup bomb threat - Federal News Network
items.summary:
The 2026 World Cup brought more than six million spectators from around the world to more than 100 matches in 16 host cities in the U.S., Canada and Mexico over the course of two months, prompting a massive interagency effort to secure those sites using technologies like AI and drones. Two people were charged in connection with another bomb threat against FIFA during a World Cup match at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. [...] A military-made artificial intelligence tool helped law enforcement thwart a bomb threat at the FIFA World Cup in California this summer.

The previously undisclosed incident occurred June 18, when Switzerland faced Bosnia and Herzegovina at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles, Army Capt. Ryan Hetrick, who leads the Pentagon’s Generative AI Task Force, said Nov. 6 at an AI event in Washington. [...] Hetrick has become one of the military’s biggest — and busiest — evangelists for AI. The GenAI Task Force travels around the globe to sit down with troops on operations floors and in the field and find AI fixes for their most pressing problems.

items.title: Australia to mandate AI breach reporting, create regulator after OpenAI breach | Reuters
items.summary:
However, both companies told Australian parliament last ​month that they would welcome ​laws requiring them to ⁠report data breaches carried out by their AI agents, acknowledging the decision to notify was currently at their discretion.

Albanese said his centre-left ​Labor government would set up an AI regulator to oversee security ​controls throughout ⁠the development and deployment of AI systems, identify serious risks and conduct independent evaluations of AI models. [...] "The AI safety regulator will be able to enforce significant penalties for AI companies ⁠doing the ​wrong thing," he said.

The mandatory AI safety and ​security protections will form part of the government's proposed AI legislation, Albanese said, which it plans to introduce in ​Parliament next year.

Reporting by Renju Jose in Sydney; Editing by Christian Schmollinger and Saad Sayeed

Our Standards: The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles. [...] OpenAI has said it learned of the breach only in August ​and that the incident was unintentional. Its review found no evidence that patient records were accessed by ‌the ⁠agent.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: FDA seeks input on telesurgery, autonomous robotics
items.summary: Rapid advances in artificial intelligence, machine learning and connectivity are driving expansion of robotic applications in a wide range of clinical settings, the FDA said. Increases in processing power, data storage and computational efficiency are enabling progress in robotic systems with autonomous capabilities. [...] In another example of teleoperation, manufacturers are developing devices that enable technicians to remotely perform ultrasounds, the FDA said. Robotic devices include stereotactic navigation systems, imaging devices and endoluminal navigation devices. [...] The FDA is asking the robotics community to submit comments on the discussion paper by Jan. 5. Ahead of that deadline, a public workshop to discuss the topics raised in the paper is scheduled for Dec. 2-3.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI kicks off charm offensive to change voters' view of data centers | Reuters
items.summary:
SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Stunning ​victories by Democrats in US midterm elections this week have been interpreted by many as Americans repudiating tech ‌industry plans to build data centers across the country. OpenAI has now embarked on new strategies to change their minds.

The AI lab on Thursday laid out policies — in the works since August — intended to help the company build more trust with local communities and convince them that data centers will ​benefit them. [...] OpenAI officials, along with many of their peers in tech, ​have spent the last ⁠two years trying to build ties with the administration of US President Donald Trump in hopes of shaping federal policy around AI.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural committee and later attended Trump's second inauguration. Last year, Brockman donated $25 million in his personal capacity to ⁠a Trump ​super PAC. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

OpenAI said it will no longer use non-disclosure agreements with public officials when negotiating or discussing future sites, although ​proprietary information would still be under wraps. It will also give residents access to construction plans ⁠and their potential effect on traffic, noise and lighting.

items.title: OpenAI will keep investing in AI data centers despite election results, CFO tells CNBC
items.summary:
OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar on Friday said the company will continue to invest in artificial intelligence infrastructure, even after voters strongly rebuked data centers during Tuesday's midterm elections. [...] OpenAI depends on data centers to train its AI models and serve customers, and Friar said she doesn't think the midterms dramatically changed anything for the company.

"If the midterm means more focus on data centers and communities, we're going to keep doing the work to get into those communities and to build trust with them," Friar said. [...] "When I think about the midterms, I need to keep thinking about how do we keep investing to meet that customer demand," Friar told CNBC's Sara Eisen in an interview at the Citi TMT Leadership Summit at California's Pebble Beach. "It starts early with having built relationships with all of the hyperscalers, and it will continue to mean that we raise capital."
